dev.repackage_data_reference.doc: Repackage a given dataset into simple parquet shards:

nanochat.checkpoint_manager.doc: Utilities for saving and loading model/optim/state checkpoints.

nanochat.core_eval.doc: Functions for evaluating the CORE metric, as described in the DCLM paper. https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11794

nanochat.dataset.doc: The base/pretraining dataset is a set of parquet files. This file contains utilities for: - iterating over the parquet files and yielding documents from it - download the files on demand if they are not on disk

nanochat.engine.doc: Engine for efficient inference of our models.

nanochat.execution.doc: Sandboxed execution utilities for running Python code that comes out of an LLM. Inspired by the OpenAI HumanEval code: https://github.com/openai/human-eval/blob/master/human_eval/execution.py

nanochat.flash_attention.doc: Unified Flash Attention interface with automatic FA3/SDPA switching.

nanochat.fp8.doc: Minimal FP8 training for nanochat — tensorwise dynamic scaling only.

nanochat.gpt.doc: GPT model (rewrite, a lot simpler) Notable features: - rotary embeddings (and no positional embeddings) - QK norm - untied weights for token embedding and lm_head - relu^2 activation in MLP - norm after token embedding - no learnable params in rmsnorm - no bias in linear layers - Group-Query Attent…

nanochat.loss_eval.doc: A number of functions that help with evaluating a base model.

nanochat.optim.doc: A nice and efficient mixed AdamW/Muon Combined Optimizer. Usually the embeddings and scalars go into AdamW, and the matrix parameters go into Muon. The same class handles both single GPU and distributed training: when there is no multi-rank process group, the communication ops are simply skipped an…

nanochat.tokenizer.doc: BPE Tokenizer in the style of GPT-4: train with rustbpe, inference with tiktoken.

scripts.base_eval.doc: Unified evaluation script for base models.

scripts.base_train.doc: Train model. From root directory of the project, run as:

scripts.chat_cli.doc: New and upgraded chat mode because a lot of the code has changed since the last one.

scripts.chat_eval.doc: Evaluate the Chat model. All the generic code lives here, and all the evaluation-specific code lives in nanochat directory and is imported from here.

scripts.chat_sft.doc: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) the model. Run as:

scripts.infer_bench.doc: Inference benchmark: measure latency, throughput, memory and bandwidth utilization of a trained checkpoint, sweeping over the decode batch size.

scripts.tok_eval.doc: Evaluate compression ratio of the tokenizer.

scripts.tok_train.doc: Train a tokenizer using our own BPE Tokenizer library. In the style of GPT-4 tokenizer.

tasks.arc.doc: The ARC dataset from Allen AI. https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/ai2_arc

tasks.common.doc: Base class for all Tasks. A Task is basically a dataset of conversations, together with some metadata and often also evaluation criteria. Example tasks: MMLU, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, GSM8K, HumanEval, SmolTalk.

tasks.humaneval.doc: Evaluate the Chat model on HumanEval dataset. Btw this dataset is a misnomer and has nothing to do with humans. It is a coding benchmark.

tasks.smoltalk.doc: SmolTalk by HuggingFace. Good "general" conversational dataset. https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceTB/smol-smoltalk We use the "smol" version, which is more appropriate for smaller models.

nanochat.checkpoint_manager:_patch_missi.doc: Add default values for new config keys missing in old checkpoints.
Add default values for new parameters that may be missing in old checkpoints.

nanochat.checkpoint_manager:build_model.doc: A bunch of repetitive code to build a model from a given checkpoint. Returns: - base model - uncompiled, not wrapped in DDP - tokenizer - meta data saved during base model training

nanochat.checkpoint_manager:load_optimiz.doc: Load just the optimizer shard for a given rank, without re-loading the model.

nanochat.common:ColoredFormatter.doc: Custom formatter that adds colors to log messages.

nanochat.common:DummyWandb.doc: Useful if we wish to not use wandb but have all the same signatures

nanochat.common:compute_cleanup.doc: Companion function to compute_init, to clean things up before script exit

nanochat.common:compute_init.doc: Basic initialization that we keep doing over and over, so make common.

nanochat.common:download_file_with_lock.doc: Downloads a file from a URL to a local path in the base directory. Uses a lock file to prevent concurrent downloads among multiple ranks.

nanochat.common:get_peak_bandwidth.doc: Peak HBM/GDDR memory bandwidth in bytes/sec. The decode phase of inference is memory-bandwidth-bound, so this is the roofline for tokens/sec (see MBU).

nanochat.common:is_ddp_initialized.doc: True if torch.distributed is available and the process group is initialized. Used at cleanup to avoid destroying a non-existent PG.

nanochat.common:is_ddp_requested.doc: True if launched by torchrun (env present), even before init. Used to decide whether we *should* initialize a PG.

nanochat.core_eval:evaluate_example.doc: Evaluate a single example, return True if correct, False otherwise

nanochat.core_eval:evaluate_task.doc: This function is responsible for evaluating one task across many examples. It also handles dispatch to all processes if the script is run with torchrun.

nanochat.core_eval:find_common_length.doc: Find the length of the common prefix or suffix across token sequences - direction: 'left' for prefix, 'right' for suffix

nanochat.core_eval:forward_model.doc: Take BxT tensor of token ids, return BxT tensor of losses and argmax predictions. The last column of losses is set to nan because we don't have autoregressive targets there.

nanochat.core_eval:render_prompts_lm.doc: Render complete prompt for a language modeling task. Notice that we manually trim the context in the template, which in some datasets seems to have trailing whitespace (which we don't want).

nanochat.core_eval:render_prompts_mc.doc: Render complete prompts for a multiple choice question

nanochat.core_eval:render_prompts_schema.doc: Render complete prompts for a schema question

nanochat.core_eval:stack_sequences.doc: Stack up a list of token sequences, pad to longest on the right

nanochat.dataloader:_document_batches.doc: Infinite iterator over document batches (list of text strings) from parquet files.

nanochat.dataloader:tokenizing_distribut.doc: Helper that omits state_dict from yields.

nanochat.dataset:download_single_file.doc: Downloads a single file index, with some backoff

nanochat.dataset:list_parquet_files.doc: Looks into a data dir and returns full paths to all parquet files.

nanochat.dataset:parquets_iter_batched.doc: Iterate through the dataset, in batches of underlying row_groups for efficiency. - split can be "train" or "val". the last parquet file will be val. - start/step are useful for skipping rows in DDP. e.g. start=rank, step=world_size

nanochat.engine:<module>.doc: Engine for efficient inference of our models.

nanochat.engine:Engine.generate.doc: Same as generate, but does single prefill and then clones the KV cache.

nanochat.engine:Engine.generate_batch.doc: Non-streaming batch generation that just returns the final token sequences. Returns a list of token sequences (list of lists of ints). Terminal tokens (assistant_end, bos) are not included in the results.

nanochat.engine:KVCache.doc: KV Cache designed for Flash Attention 3's flash_attn_with_kvcache API.

nanochat.engine:KVCache.advance.doc: Advance the cache position by num_tokens.

nanochat.engine:KVCache.get_layer_cache.doc: Return (k_cache, v_cache) views for a specific layer.

nanochat.engine:KVCache.get_pos.doc: Get current position (assumes all batch elements at same position).

nanochat.engine:KVCache.prefill.doc: Copy cached KV from another cache into this one. Used when we do batch=1 prefill and then want to generate multiple samples in parallel.

nanochat.engine:sample_next_token.doc: Sample a single next token from given logits of shape (B, vocab_size). Returns (B, 1).

nanochat.engine:use_calculator.doc: Evaluate a Python expression safely. Supports both math expressions and string operations like .count()

nanochat.execution:ExecutionResult.doc: Result of executing Python code in a sandbox.

nanochat.execution:execute_code.doc: Execute Python code in a sandboxed environment.

nanochat.flash_attention:_resolve_use_fa.doc: Decide once whether to use FA3, based on availability, override, and dtype.

nanochat.flash_attention:_sdpa_attention.doc: SDPA attention with sliding window support. q, k, v are (B, H, T, D) format.

nanochat.flash_attention:flash_attn_func.doc: Flash Attention for training (no KV cache).

nanochat.flash_attention:flash_attn_with.doc: Flash Attention with KV cache for inference.

nanochat.fp8:Float8Linear.doc: Drop-in nn.Linear replacement that does FP8 compute.

nanochat.fp8:Float8Linear.from_float.doc: Create Float8Linear from nn.Linear, sharing the same weight and bias.

nanochat.fp8:Float8LinearConfig.doc: Minimal config matching torchao's API. Only tensorwise recipe is supported.

nanochat.fp8:_Float8Matmul.doc: Custom autograd for the three FP8 GEMMs of a Linear layer.

nanochat.fp8:_to_col_major.doc: Rearrange a 2D tensor's memory to column-major layout.

nanochat.fp8:_to_fp8.doc: Dynamically quantize a tensor to FP8 using tensorwise scaling.

nanochat.fp8:convert_to_float8_training.doc: Replace nn.Linear layers with Float8Linear throughout a module.

nanochat.gpt:GPT.__init__.doc: NOTE a major footgun: this __init__ function runs in meta device context (!!) Therefore, any calculations inside here are shapes and dtypes only, no actual data. => We actually initialize all data (parameters, buffers, etc.) in init_weights() instead.

nanochat.gpt:GPT._compute_window_sizes.doc: Compute per-layer window sizes for sliding window attention.

nanochat.gpt:GPT.estimate_decode_flops.doc: Forward FLOPs to decode one token at a given context length during inference: 2 FLOPs per matmul param, plus attention over min(context, window) per layer.

nanochat.gpt:GPT.estimate_flops.doc: Return the estimated FLOPs per token for the model (forward + backward). Each matmul weight parameter contributes 2 FLOPs (multiply *, accumulate +) in forward, and 2X that in backward => 2+4=6. Cleanest explanation of this: https://medium.com/@dzmitrybahdanau/the-flops-calculus-of-language-model-t…

nanochat.gpt:GPT.estimate_prefill_flops.doc: Forward FLOPs to prefill a prompt: causal, so token t attends to min(t, window).

nanochat.gpt:GPT.generate.doc: Naive autoregressive streaming inference. To make it super simple, let's assume: - batch size is 1 - ids and the yielded tokens are simple Python lists and ints

nanochat.gpt:GPT.init_weights.doc: Initialize the full model in this one function for maximum clarity.

nanochat.gpt:GPT.kv_bytes_per_token.doc: Bytes to *store* one token of KV cache during inference, per row (all layers).

nanochat.gpt:GPT.kv_read_bytes.doc: Bytes of KV cache *read* by one decode step at a given context length, per row. Sliding window layers only attend to (and read) the last `window` tokens.

nanochat.gpt:GPT.num_matmul_params.doc: The number of parameters that participate in matmuls with the token stream, i.e. contribute 2 FLOPs/param to the forward pass. Counted structurally: every matmul in this model goes through the Linear class, while non-matmul params (embeddings = lookups, per-layer scalars) are nn.Embedding or raw Pa…

nanochat.gpt:GPT.num_scaling_params.doc: Return detailed parameter counts for scaling law analysis. Different papers use different conventions: - Kaplan et al. excluded embedding parameters - Chinchilla included all parameters Ref: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15556 (Chinchilla paper) Ref: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.08361 (Kaplan et al. ori…

nanochat.gpt:Linear.doc: nn.Linear that casts weights to match input dtype in forward. Replaces autocast: master weights stay fp32 for optimizer precision, but matmuls run in the activation dtype (typically bf16 from embeddings).

nanochat.gpt:has_ve.doc: Returns True if GPT layer should have Value Embedding (alternating, last layer always included).

nanochat.loss_eval:evaluate_bpb.doc: Instead of the naive 'mean loss', this function returns the bits per byte (bpb), which is a tokenization vocab size-independent metric, meaning you are still comparing apples:apples if you change the vocab size. The way this works is that instead of just calculating the average loss as usual, you c…

nanochat.optim:MuonAdamW.doc: Combined optimizer: Muon for 2D matrix params, AdamW for others.

nanochat.optim:MuonAdamW._compute_adamw.doc: Wait for reduce, compute AdamW updates, launch gathers for large params.

nanochat.optim:MuonAdamW._compute_muon.doc: Wait for reduce, compute Muon updates, launch gather.

nanochat.optim:MuonAdamW._finish_gathers.doc: Wait for all gathers and copy Muon params back.

nanochat.optim:MuonAdamW._reduce_adamw.doc: Launch async reduce ops for AdamW group. Returns info dict with per-param infos.

nanochat.optim:MuonAdamW._reduce_muon.doc: Launch async reduce op for Muon group. Returns info dict.

nanochat.optim:adamw_step_fused.doc: Fused AdamW step: weight_decay -> momentum_update -> bias_correction -> param_update All in one compiled graph to eliminate Python overhead between ops. The 0-D CPU tensors avoid recompilation when hyperparameter values change.

nanochat.optim:muon_step_fused.doc: Fused Muon step: momentum -> polar_express -> variance_reduction -> cautious_update All in one compiled graph to eliminate Python overhead between ops. Some of the constants are 0-D CPU tensors to avoid recompilation when values change.

nanochat.tokenizer:RustBPETokenizer.doc: Light wrapper around tiktoken (for efficient inference) but train with rustbpe

nanochat.tokenizer:RustBPETokenizer.rend.doc: Tokenize a single Chat conversation (which we call a "doc" or "document" here). Returns: - ids: list[int] is a list of token ids of this rendered conversation - mask: list[int] of same length, mask = 1 for tokens that the Assistant is expected to train on.
Used during Reinforcement Learning. In that setting, we want to render the conversation priming the Assistant for a completion. Unlike the Chat SFT case, we don't need to return the mask.

nanochat.tokenizer:RustBPETokenizer.visu.doc: Small helper function useful in debugging: visualize the tokenization of render_conversation

scripts.base_eval:evaluate_core.doc: Evaluate a base model on the CORE benchmark. Returns dict with results, centered_results, and core_metric.

scripts.base_eval:place_eval_bundle.doc: Unzip eval_bundle.zip and place it in the base directory.

scripts.base_train:<module>.doc: Train model. From root directory of the project, run as:

scripts.base_train:build_model_meta.doc: Build a model on meta device for a given depth (shapes/dtypes only, no data).

scripts.base_train:disable_fp8.doc: Temporarily swap Float8Linear modules with nn.Linear for BF16 evaluation.

scripts.chat_cli:<module>.doc: New and upgraded chat mode because a lot of the code has changed since the last one.

scripts.chat_eval:<module>.doc: Evaluate the Chat model. All the generic code lives here, and all the evaluation-specific code lives in nanochat directory and is imported from here.

scripts.chat_rl:run_gsm8k_eval.doc: Evaluates GSM8K task and returns a list of records of evaluation outcomes. In a distributed setting, all ranks cooperate but this function will NOT do the reduction across ranks. This is the responsibility of the caller. Because the evaluation can take a while, this function will yield records one …

scripts.chat_sft:<module>.doc: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) the model. Run as:

scripts.chat_sft:sft_data_generator_bos_.doc: BOS-aligned dataloader for SFT with bestfit-pad packing.

scripts.infer_bench:bench_generate.doc: Run one timed generation. Returns dict of measurements.

scripts.infer_bench:build_prompt.doc: A natural-language prompt of exactly num_tokens tokens (random ids would do for speed, but a real prompt keeps argmax decoding from degenerating).

scripts.infer_bench:weight_bytes.doc: Bytes of parameters as stored (each decode step reads all of them).

scripts.tok_eval:<module>.doc: Evaluate compression ratio of the tokenizer.

scripts.tok_eval:print_comparison.doc: Print comparison table between baseline tokenizer and ours.

scripts.tok_train:<module>.doc: Train a tokenizer using our own BPE Tokenizer library. In the style of GPT-4 tokenizer.

scripts.tok_train:text_iterator.doc: 1) Flatten the batches into a single iterator 2) Crop every document to args.doc_cap characters 3) Break when we've seen args.max_chars characters

tasks.common:HubDataset.doc: Minimal stand-in for a HuggingFace datasets Dataset: wraps a pyarrow Table and offers lazy row access and a seeded shuffle.

tasks.common:Task.doc: Base class of a Task. Allows for lightweight slicing of the underlying dataset.

tasks.common:TaskMixture.doc: For SFT Training it becomes useful to train on a mixture of datasets. Fun trick: if you wish to oversample any task, just pass it in multiple times in the list.

tasks.common:TaskMixture.get_example.doc: Access conversations according to a deterministic shuffle of all examples. This ensures tasks are mixed throughout training, regardless of dataset size.

tasks.common:TaskSequence.doc: For SFT Training sometimes we want to sequentially train on a list of tasks. This is useful for cases that require a training curriculum.

tasks.common:load_hub_dataset.doc: Minimal stand-in for HuggingFace datasets.load_dataset(repo_id, subset, split=split). Every dataset on the hub has an auto-generated parquet export. We list the parquet shards via the hub API, download them (once) into the local cache directory, and read them with pyarrow. Under torchrun, only one …

tasks.common:render_mc.doc: The common multiple choice rendering format we will use.

tasks.gsm8k:GSM8K.evaluate.doc: Given (conversation, completion), return evaluation outcome (0 = wrong, 1 = correct) Note that: - the conversation has both user AND assistant message (containing the ground truth answer) - the assistant_response is usually the alternative assistant message achieved via sampling

tasks.gsm8k:GSM8K.get_example.doc: Get a single problem from the dataset.

tasks.gsm8k:GSM8K.reward.doc: Used during RL. To keep things simple, just re-use the evaluation above. Later this could be made more complex (e.g. format matching etc.)

tasks.gsm8k:extract_answer.doc: Extract the numerical answer after #### marker. Follows official code for normalization: https://github.com/openai/grade-school-math/blob/3101c7d5072418e28b9008a6636bde82a006892c/grade_school_math/dataset.py#L28

tasks.humaneval:HumanEval.evaluate.doc: Given (conversation, completion), return boolean success of the completion.

tasks.humaneval:HumanEval.get_example.doc: Get a single problem from the dataset.

tasks.humaneval:extract_imports.doc: Extract import statements from the beginning of a code block.

tasks.humaneval:extract_program.doc: Extract Python code from LLM completion.

tasks.smoltalk:SmolTalk.doc: smol-smoltalk dataset. train is 460K rows, test is 24K rows.
